items.label: SPY5 + SPYL (S&P 500 duplication)
items.detail: SPY5 ($223,473.60, 45.65% of NAV) and SPYL ($119,857.92, 24.49% of NAV) both track the S&P 500 and together total $343,331.52 = 70.14% of the $489,492.21 NAV (source: get_account_positions, get_account_summary, live 2026-08-31 15:31 UTC). Computed 1-year daily-return correlation between the two is +0.9929 (n=253, get_price_history closes Aug 2025-Aug 2026).
items.recommendation: Trim SPYL (the smaller, more redundant leg) by roughly half -- approx. 3,120 of 6,240 shares (~$59,929 at the $19.208 last price) -- and redeploy into SHY (iShares 1-3Y Treasury), which showed the lowest correlation to both SPY5 (-0.0471) and SPYL (-0.0358) of six hedge candidates tested (IEF +0.007/+0.014, TLT +0.026/+0.025, AGG +0.031/+0.037, EFA +0.267/+0.267, VXUS +0.261/+0.263).

items.label: Zero fixed-income ballast ahead of a possible September Fed hike
items.detail: get_pa_allocation (live) shows 0% of NAV in bonds -- 80.98% ETFs, 13.10% direct equities, 5.92% cash, no duration exposure anywhere. The Fed held rates at 3.50-3.75% on Jul 29, 2026 in a divided 9-3 vote (three officials wanted a hike); Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Aug 28, 2026 remarks that inflation 'remains too high' pushed market-implied odds of a September 16 hike to roughly 57%, up from about 40% pre-speech (sources: cambridgecurrencies.com Fed calendar; CBS News Fed outlook; Yahoo Finance Aug 28 2026 market recap).
items.recommendation: Establish a Treasury ballast (SHY and/or IEF) sized at roughly 5% of NAV (~$24,500); both showed near-zero correlation to the account's largest equity holdings (SHY -0.047 vs SPY5, IEF +0.007 vs SPY5), making them the most effective shock absorbers identified in this analysis if the Fed surprises hawkish on Sept 16.

items.label: Available trading funds ($208.72) vs. reported cash balance ($28,311.97)
items.detail: get_account_summary (live) reports total_cash_value $28,311.97 (5.78% of NAV) but available_funds and buying_power of only $208.72; excess_liquidity is separately reported at $28,311.97 -- an inconsistency in the raw IBKR data worth confirming directly in the platform before placing new orders.
items.recommendation: Verify true buying power in the IBKR client before funding any hedge position with fresh cash. If available funds are genuinely near-zero, fund the SHY/IEF additions recommended here by trimming SPYL and/or the precious-metals cluster rather than deploying new capital.

items.label: Precious-metals / mining cluster (IGLN, SSLV, KGC, NEM)
items.detail: IGLN ($41,294.48, 8.44%), SSLV ($7,771.48, 1.59%), KGC ($5,356.57, 1.09%) and NEM ($5,909.31, 1.21%) total $60,331.84 = 12.33% of NAV (get_account_positions, live). Gold trades near $4,452/oz as of late Aug 2026, well off its Jan 29, 2026 all-time high of $5,595; Goldman Sachs, HSBC, JPMorgan and StoneX have all cut year-end 2026 gold targets to a $4,000-$4,900 range on dollar strength and a hawkish Fed, with ING projecting just a $4,300 average for Q3 2026 (sources: goldrepublic.com, jpmorgan.com gold research, Aug 2026).
items.recommendation: Add IEF (iShares 7-10Y Treasury) as the cluster hedge: IGLN's 1-year correlation to IEF is +0.072, the lowest of six candidates tested (SHY +0.075, TLT +0.083, AGG +0.079, EFA +0.139, VXUS +0.153) -- pairing the metals cluster with a rate-sensitive Treasury bucket offsets a hawkish-Fed / stronger-dollar shock to gold without abandoning the position.

items.label: AI-infrastructure pair (CRWV, GEV) trades as one factor
items.detail: CRWV ($12,523.50, 2.56% of NAV, -$278.50 unrealized) and GEV ($8,924.80, 1.82% of NAV, -$824.10 unrealized) show a 1-year daily-return correlation of +0.43 (n=250, get_price_history closes) -- both are geared to AI-datacenter capex. NVIDIA's Aug 27, 2026 blowout Q2 (EPS $2.22 vs $2.09 est., revenue $96.22B, FY28 growth guidance raised to 70%) drove an 8.7% NVDA rally the next session and lifted the broader AI trade, underscoring how tightly this pair rides the same single-stock catalyst (source: get_account_positions live; Yahoo Finance/Zacks Aug 28 2026 market recap).
items.recommendation: Trim CRWV specifically (the pair's higher-volatility, less rate-insulated leg) by 30-50%, or lean on the SHY ballast above: a dollar-weighted CRWV/GEV blend (58.4%/41.6%) shows a -0.057 correlation to SHY, the lowest of six hedge candidates tested for this pair (IEF +0.005, TLT +0.015, AGG +0.061, EFA +0.425, VXUS +0.482).
